As it currently stands
column2: skb destructors are forbidden on the

column1: receive path because the protocol end-points will overwrite
any existing destructor with their own.
This is the reason why we have to call skb_orphan in the loopback
driver before we reinject the packet back into the stack
creating a period during which loopback traffic isn't charged
to any socket.
With virtualisation
column2: we have a similar problem in that traffic

column1: is reinjected into the stack without being associated with any
socket entity
column2: thus providing no natural congestion push-back

column1: for those poor folks still stuck with UDP.
Now had we been consistent in telling them that UDP simply has
no congestion feedback
column2: I could just fob them off.  Unfortunately

column1: we appear to have gone to some length in catering for this on
the standard UDP path
column2: with skb/socket accounting so that has

column1: created a very unhealthy dependency.
Alas habits are difficult to break out of
to allow skb destructors on the receive path.
It turns out that making skb destructors useable on the receive path
isn't as easy as it seems.  For instance
to skb_set_owner_r isn't enough.  This is because we assume all
over the IP stack that skb->sk is an IP socket if present.
The new transparent proxy code goes one step further and assumes
that skb->sk is the receiving socket if present.
Now all of this can be dealt with by adding simple checks such
as only treating skb->sk as an IP socket if skb->sk->sk_family
matches.  However
column2: it turns out that for bridging at least we

column1: don't need to do all of this work.
This is of interest because most virtualisation setups use bridging
so we don't actually go through the IP stack on the host (with
the exception of our old nemesis the bridge netfilter
easily taken care of).
So this patch simply adds skb_orphan to the point just before we
enter the IP stack
column2: but after we've gone through the bridge on the

column1: receive path.  It also adds an skb_orphan to the one place in
netfilter that touches skb->sk/skb->destructor
One word of caution
column2: because of the internal code structure

column1: wishing to deploy this must use skb_set_owner_w as opposed to
skb_set_owner_r since many functions that create a new skb from
an existing one will invoke skb_set_owner_w on the new skb.
